title: Queen vs Rook: Philidor's Position (1777)
description: Philidor (1777): White's pieces are ideally placed. Win by Queen triangulation (1.Qe5+ Ka7 2.Qa1+ Kb8 3.Qa5!) to force Black into zugzwang, driving the Rook away to land a decisive double attack.
theoryNotes: 1. Triangulation: White plays 1.Qe5+ Ka7 2.Qa1+ Kb8 3.Qa5! to pass the move back to Black. 2. Zugzwang: The black rook must abandon the king (e.g. 3...Rb1 or 3...Rh7). 3. Double Attack (Fork): After 3...Rb1, 4.Qd8+ Ka7 5.Qd4+ Ka8 6.Qh8+ Ka7 7.Qh7+ forks King and Rook to win 8.Qxb1.
keyTip: Execute the Queen triangle: e5 → a1 → a5! Keep Black's King locked on the rim and watch out for stalemate sacrifices.

title: Queen vs Rook: Herding from Center (13-3)
description: Herding a solitary rook defense from the open center. Coordinate Queen and King to push the defender to the flank, avoid perpetual checks, and convert within 50 moves.
theoryNotes: Under modern time controls, Q vs R frequently ends in 50-move draws when the attacker misplaces the Queen (e.g. Svidler vs Gelfand 2001). Use precise geometric checks (2.Qd4+, 3.Qg4+, 4.Qe6+) to herd the defending King to the rim while bringing your King up.
keyTip: Keep the Queen controlling diagonal cross-files and advance your King as soon as the defending King is restricted.

title: Queen vs Bishop-Pawn on 7th
description: Defend the pawn on the 7th rank against the Queen by exploiting the stalemate defense in the corner.
theoryNotes: Bishop pawns (c-pawn / f-pawn) and Rook pawns (a-pawn / h-pawn) on the 7th rank with the defending King in front or beside the pawn are theoretical draws if the opposing King is too far.
keyTip: Step into the corner (a1/h1/a8/h8) whenever checked to threaten a stalemate if the Queen captures.

title: The Lucena Position (Building the Bridge)
description: The quintessential winning rook endgame technique. Use your rook to build a bridge and shield your King from vertical checks.
theoryNotes: 1. Place your rook on the 4th rank (Rb4). 2. Step your King out of the queening square. 3. Interpose with your rook on the 4th rank when Black checks from behind.
keyTip: Remember: 'Rook to the 4th rank!' (e.g. Rb4). Once checked on the 5th rank, your King steps to the 4th, and Rb4-e4 blocks the check.

title: The Philidor Defense (6th Rank Hold)
description: The golden standard for drawing rook endgames down a pawn. Cut off the enemy King from the 6th rank.
theoryNotes: 1. Keep your rook on the 6th rank (or 3rd rank if Black) to prevent the enemy King from advancing. 2. As soon as the pawn advances, immediately swing your rook to the 1st rank and deliver endless checks from behind.
keyTip: Do not leave the 6th rank until White physically advances their pawn!

title: The Vancura Defense (Flank Checks)
description: Defend against a passed rook pawn by anchoring your rook on the flank and checking the enemy King horizontally.
theoryNotes: When the attacker has an a-pawn or h-pawn on the 6th/7th rank, the defending rook attacks the pawn from the side (f6/g6 or b3/c3) and gives side checks whenever the King steps out.
keyTip: Keep distance between your rook and the enemy King so you cannot be harassed or trapped.

title: Key Squares & Direct Opposition
description: Seize the direct opposition with your King in front of your passed pawn to escort it to promotion.
theoryNotes: If your King reaches the key squares in front of the pawn (e.g. d5, e5, f5 when pawn is on e4), the win is guaranteed. Take the opposition whenever the Kings are separated by one odd square.
keyTip: Always keep your King ahead of your pawn, not behind it!

title: Triangulation & Passing the Move
description: Defend against the opponent's outflanking attempts by holding key critical defensive squares.
theoryNotes: Triangulation is a triangular maneuver by the King (e.g. d3-c3-d2-d3) to lose a tempo and hand the turn to the opponent, forcing them into zugzwang.
keyTip: Calculate which square corresponds to the opponent's king position before committing.

title: Bishop & Knight Checkmate (W-Manoeuvre)
description: The ultimate test of coordination. Drive the lone King into a corner that matches the color of your Bishop using the W-shaped Knight path.
theoryNotes: 1. Checkmate can ONLY be forced in a corner matching your Bishop's square color. 2. The Knight controls squares of opposite color to the Bishop. 3. The Knight follows a W-path (e.g. f2-d3-e5-c6-b8) to herd the King.
keyTip: Keep the 50-move rule in mind! Avoid letting the enemy king slip out between your pieces into the center.

title: Two Bishops Checkmate
description: Trap the enemy King between two adjacent bishop diagonals, push it to any edge, and deliver checkmate.
theoryNotes: Bishops work best side-by-side (e.g. d3 and e3) to create an impassable laser wall. Advance your King behind the wall to push the opponent back rank by rank.
keyTip: Bring your King into the action early to cut off escape routes.

title: Rook vs Bishop: The Safe Corner Defense
description: Exploit the 'wrong corner' trap where the Bishop's color does not match the corner square to win the piece or deliver mate.
theoryNotes: In Rook vs Bishop, the defending King must run to the 'Safe Corner' (a corner of the OPPOSITE color of their Bishop). If forced into the 'Wrong Corner' (same color as Bishop), they will be mated or lose the Bishop.
keyTip: Trap the King and Bishop on the same diagonal file to win material.
